record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Does there exist a simple (OR)*-group, where an (OR)*-group is a right-orderable group in which every right partial order extends to a right order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A right order on a group $G$ is a total order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a\le b$ implies $ac\le bc$ for all $a,b,c\in G$. A right partial order on $G$ is a partial order that is right-invariant in the same sense. A group $G$ is called right-orderable if it admits at least one right order. Define an $(OR)^*$-group to be a right-orderable group $G$ with the additional property that every right partial order on $G$ can be extended to a (total) right order on $G$.

Question: Does there exist a simple $(OR)^*$-group?
artifact.status_search_result: No source located that resolves the existence of a simple $(OR)^*$-group. The problem is listed among unsolved problems on orderable groups, and related results (e.g., Medvedev's work showing the class of right-orderable groups does not coincide with the axiomatic closure of $(OR)^*$, and the existence of simple groups whose partial orders extend to lattice orders) appear in the literature but do not settle this specific question.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an unsolved problem on right-orderable groups.

status_evidence.title: Ordering groups and validity in lattice-ordered groups
status_evidence.snippet: inductive characterization of subsets of a group that extend to the positive cone of a right order
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies extendability of partial right orders to right orders but does not resolve existence of a simple (OR)*-group.
